article.title: Apache Roller XML-RPC Deserialization Flaw Resurfaces as CVE-2026-129448, Now Under Active Exploitation
article.summary: A September fix for Apache Roller's XML-RPC deserialization bug covered only one version; the flaw got a new CVE covering 4.0.0-6.1.4 and is now being actively exploited.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Apache Roller, an open-source blogging platform written in Java, according to [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/203419/security/apache-roller-rce-flaw-cve-2026-129448-under-active-attack.html), has a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw that is being actively exploited, the Apache Software Foundation disclosed. The flaw, tracked as [CVE-2026-129448](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q), is a near-duplicate of a bug for which Apache had already shipped a narrower fix in September, and this time the foundation says the affected range is far larger than it first reported.

## What We Know

The [GitHub Security Advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q) describes the issue as "Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4" that "allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code," because "the XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester." The flaw carries a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8, according to both [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/critical-apache-roller-rce-flaw-under.html) and the [GitHub advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q).

Apache says CVE-2026-129448 "is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected," according to the [GitHub advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q), and that "this issue is being actively exploited," according to both [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/apache-warns-of-roller-rce-vulnerability-exploited-in-attacks/) and the [GitHub advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q). Neither Apache nor the outlets covering the disclosure specified when the exploitation began, which attackers are behind it, or which organizations have been targeted.

The original, narrower issue, [CVE-2026-82384](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rhg-vvf7-p29p), was disclosed on the oss-security mailing list on September 25, 2026, in a post from Apache Roller committer David M. Johnson, according to [the mailing list archive](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/09/25/17). That advisory credited researcher n0mi1k with the discovery and described a flaw limited to version 6.1.5, in which "the servlet is mapped unconditionally, so parsing occurs even when the global XML-RPC feature is set to disabled," according to the [GitHub advisory for CVE-2026-82384](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rhg-vvf7-p29p). The fix merged into the Roller codebase on September 5, 2026, under the title "Disable vendor extension types on the XML-RPC servlet," according to [the pull request](https://github.com/apache/roller/pull/171), on the reasoning that "a disabled API is closed at the endpoint instead of relying on per-handler checks," per the same pull request.

n0mi1k is again credited with discovering the broader issue behind CVE-2026-129448, with Matt Raible credited as the one who reported it to the project, according to both [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/critical-apache-roller-rce-flaw-under.html) and [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/203419/security/apache-roller-rce-flaw-cve-2026-129448-under-active-attack.html). Raible had already reviewed and approved the original fix in [pull request #171](https://github.com/apache/roller/pull/171) in September, before the broader scope of the issue was identified.

Apache recommends upgrading to Roller 6.1.6 or later, which "disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled," according to the [GitHub advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q). For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, the advisory recommends setting "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or removing the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping and restarting Roller, according to both [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/apache-warns-of-roller-rce-vulnerability-exploited-in-attacks/) and the [GitHub advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxp4-phq9-fx2q). The advisory specifically warns that "disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting," a caveat also noted by [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/203419/security/apache-roller-rce-flaw-cve-2026-129448-under-active-attack.html).

[NVD's record for CVE-2026-129448](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-129448) lists the advisory as published on November 17, 2026, a day before BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and Security Affairs reported on it on November 18.

## What We Don't Know

Apache has not disclosed when attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-129448, what techniques they are using, or which organizations, if any, have been compromised. It also remains unclear how long the broader 4.0.0-6.1.4 version range was vulnerable before the September patch, released only for 6.1.5, left most other affected versions unaddressed, or how Apache identified that the fix needed to cover additional versions.
